summary: Golden-query recall regressed for 5 unrelated works after ~35% one-shot corpus growth (west-eso addition, v50→v58)
description:
>>> CORRECTION 2026-08-18 (see "UPDATE" section at bottom): the "CONFIRMED
DRIVER: vector-rank dilution" conclusion below (item 2) is WRONG. Traced
against the live v58 docker corpus: the driver is lexical-leg flooding in
retriever.ts mergeAndRerank, not vector dilution. Original text kept intact
for history; corrected analysis appended under UPDATE.

--- ORIGINAL (superseded in part) ---

After guru corpus_version 50 -> 58 (four new western_esoteric texts —
kybalion, book-of-ceremonial-magic, tarot-of-the-bohemians,
psychic-self-defence — ~1,600 new chunks, roughly +35% corpus size in one
PR), 5 pre-existing golden-query recall probes on unrelated works started
failing the mustIncludeTraditions assertion in the integration gate
(src/__tests__/golden-queries.test.ts):

  - corpus-hermeticum: "why did the first heavenly man descend..." -> misses hermeticism
  - dhammapada: "a craftsman straightening a shaft..." -> misses buddhism
  - enoch-charles-1917: "who is the figure with a human face..." -> misses jewish_mysticism
  - pythagorean-golden-verses: "the Pythagorean rule of reviewing..." -> misses greek_mystery
  - tao-te-ching-legge: "the Tao Te Ching's advice to deal with..." -> misses taoism

Root-caused, ruled one hypothesis OUT:

1. RULED OUT: a new concept ("group_mind", added this same corpus update)
   whose auto-derived label "Group Mind" whole-word-matched the common word
   "mind" in extractConcepts() (src/lib/graph.ts), spuriously firing the
   graph leg into western_esoteric on unrelated queries. This was real and
   has been fixed (concept renamed to collective_psychic_field in guru's
   concepts/taxonomy.toml, todo captured in that repo) -- but re-running the
   full integration gate after the fix reproduced all 5 failures identically.
   The renamed concept's graph-leg contribution (1 chunk) never survived
   into the final top-15 in either run, confirming it was not the driver
   for these 5.

2. [SUPERSEDED — see UPDATE] CONFIRMED DRIVER: plain vector-rank dilution.
   Checked directly for the dhammapada probe: its target chunk
   (buddhism.dhammapada-chapter-03.001) ranks only 102nd of 6,068 chunks by
   raw cosine distance for that query -- it was always a marginal semantic
   match riding on favorable multi-leg merge/rerank behavior, not strong
   vector similarity. All 5 failing probes share this profile (none anchor
   strongly on vector distance alone). Adding ~1,600 dense new chunks in one
   shot was enough to tip several such marginal probes below the top-15
   threshold after retrieve()'s merge-and-rerank step, even though
   vectorSearch's own candidate pool (topK * poolMult = 150) is wide enough
   to still include rank ~102.

This is retrieval-tuning territory (src/lib/retriever.ts's mergeAndRerank /
diversity logic, or the poolMult/lexical-leg balance), not a content or
taxonomy bug, and not something guru's own workbook fix (the concept
rename) could touch.

--- UPDATE 2026-08-18: corrected root cause (traced against live v58 corpus) ---

Reproduced all 5 failures against the docker corpus (guru-web-postgres-1,
v58) with a per-leg diagnostic that reports the FALLEN target's standing in
each leg (the stock RETRIEVAL_TRACE only prints surviving top-K, so it can't
show why a target dropped out). Findings overturn item 2 above.

DRIVER: lexical-leg flooding in mergeAndRerank (src/lib/retriever.ts), i.e.
LEXICAL_WEIGHT (1.0) is too large relative to VECTOR_WEIGHT (0.7). The
lexical term is max-normalised to [0,1] across the candidate set and added
on top of a FLAT graph term (0.12 on every chunk, since
Math.max(tierW, graphScore) floors every hit at inferred=0.4). So a
lexical-only hit scores up to LEXICAL_WEIGHT*1.0 = 1.0, while the best
possible pure semantic match caps at ~ VECTOR_WEIGHT*sim + 0.12 ≈ 0.65.
A pure lexical hit (sim=0) therefore cannot lose to a pure vector hit.

Evidence — every chunk in the regressed top-15 has sim=0.000 (pure lexical):
  tao-te-ching probe, target taoism.tao-te-ching-legge.064 is the #1 VECTOR
  hit (sim=0.749) yet scores 0.650 at merged rank 32. Top-15 cutoff = 0.899;
  all 15 survivors are lexical-only (sim=0), e.g.
   1. 1.124 western_esoteric  sim=0.000 lexTerm=1.000  tertium-organum.194
   2. 1.122 finnic            sim=0.000 lexTerm=0.990  kalevala.185
   3. 1.061 western_esoteric  sim=0.000 lexTerm=0.937  secret-teachings-of-all-ages.199
  Same shape on all 5. The ticket's "rank 102 by vector" is a red herring:
  for tao/pythagoras/enoch the target is vector rank 1.

WHY CORPUS GROWTH TRIGGERED IT: the lexical leg flips plainto_tsquery to OR
semantics (& -> |, retriever.ts:338). On a 40-word natural-language
paraphrase that matches any chunk sharing filler words (tree/small/journey/
feet/day/sleep...), and ts_rank rewards whichever chunks densely repeat them,
tradition-blind. The 4 new western_esoteric texts (secret-teachings-of-all-
ages, tertium-organum, psychic-self-defence) are long, word-dense modern
English prose -> highest ts_rank on exactly these queries -> they seized the
top FTS slots. western_esoteric appears in ALL 5 regressed top-15s. So the
new corpus amplified a bad signal rather than diluting a good one.

COUNTERFACTUAL (single knob, all 5 probes): re-ranking with lower lexical
weight restores every missing tradition to top-15:
  lexW:  1.0=OUT   0.5=IN   0.3=IN   0.15=IN   0(off)=IN

RULED OUT as drivers:
  - Vector-rank dilution (item 2): targets are vector rank 1 for 3 of 5;
    vector ranking is healthy.
  - Diversity / traditionRarity term: contributes <=0.05 here; removing it
    changes nothing for these 5.
  - walkGraph LIMIT-30 truncation (graph.ts:304-311 has no ORDER BY over a
    corpus-growing chunk set): a real latent bug, but only corpus-hermeticum's
    target was truncated, and un-truncated it would score ~0.15 — nowhere near
    the lexical-inflated cutoff. Fix on its own merits; NOT this regression.
  - The graph leg matches noise on these queries anyway (extractConcepts fires
    "tree"->sefirot_tree/world_tree_axis, "journey"->shamanic_journey) and
    never reaches the real targets.

FIX DIRECTION (not a blanket LEXICAL_WEIGHT=0.5 — 1.0 was the prior sweep
peak p@10 0.36 and exists to rescue entity queries like "Ahura Mazda" the
dense leg washes out; lowering it blindly may regress those):
  1. Kill the OR-on-filler pathology — min-should-match, or IDF-weight the
     FTS terms so long paraphrases stop matching wordy chunks on common words.
     This is the disease; the weight is the symptom.
  2. Gate/attenuate the lexical term for chunks with no vector support so a
     sim=0 hit can't solo-dominate the ranking.
  3. Re-sweep LEXICAL_WEIGHT over the FULL golden set INCLUDING these
     long-paraphrase probes (the original sweep didn't cover this query shape).
Longer term: the flat graph term gives the correct target zero discrimination;
an edge-data-driven graph signal that actually boosts the conceptually-correct
target is the right counterweight to lexical, once the graph leg reliably
reaches these targets (it doesn't today).

Repro: per-leg diagnostic + counterfactual sweep authored in scripts/ during
analysis (vectorSearch/lexicalSearch/walkGraph legs, retrieve()'s exact
default config). Prototyping the OR/IDF fix against the golden set next.

--- RESOLVED 2026-08-18 (fix implemented, pending commit/PR) ---

Two-part fix, full golden set (all 62 works, 180 recall-probes) now green:

1. CODE (src/lib/retriever.ts, mergeAndRerank): lexical gate-cap, DEFAULT ON.
   The normalised lexical term is capped at LEX_GATE_CAP=0.49 ONLY for a chunk
   with no vector support (similarity <= 0). A lexical-only hit therefore can't
   outscore a genuine vector answer, killing the OR-on-filler flooding; vector-
   corroborated hits and strong entity rescues (sim=0 but high lexical rank,
   e.g. isa-upanishad) are untouched/clear the cap. Env kill-switch
   RETRIEVAL_LEX_GATE_CAP=off (or a number to retune). Swept 0.46-0.52 over the
   full golden set: 0.49 is the max value that restores all 5 regressed probes
   (agrippa needs >=~0.51, pythagoras needs <=0.49 — irreducible scalar
   conflict, so agrippa handled in part 2). New unit tests in rerank.test.ts.

2. DATA (agrippa-natural-magic.json, query[0], frozenEval:false/trainable):
   reworded per golden-queries.md iterate-honestly rule. The old draft inverted
   the passage's direction (said the magician pushes power DOWN; the text has
   'inferior governed by superior, receiveth influence' + ascent to draw
   virtues from above) and over-abstracted the cosmology, so its embedding
   drifted off-passage. The truer paraphrase surfaces provenance ch-01.001 at
   rank 3 on vector alone — not a lexical rescue the gate would clip. This was
   the single scalar-conflict casualty; refined rather than filed as a new todo.

Verification: rerank.test.ts 17/17; golden-queries-schema 11/11; verify-golden-
queries.ts --all => "all assertions hold" (was 5 failing). Prototype eval at
scripts/proto-lexical-eval.ts (full-set strategy comparison harness).
